prerequisites.title: Multiplying a Matrix by a Column Vector

sections.markdown:
Every linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ that acts on 2D-vectors has a $2 \times 2$ matrix $T$ associated with it. The matrix is called the **standard matrix** of the linear transformation. For any vector $\mathbf{v},$ the standard matrix $T$ of a linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ must have the property $$ \mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}) = T \cdot \mathbf{v} $$ where $T \cdot \mathbf{v}$ is the matrix product of the standard matrix $T$ and the vector $\mathbf{v}.$ To illustrate, consider the following linear transformation: $$ \mathbf{S}: \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} \longrightarrow \begin{bmatrix}-3x+7y \\ x-5y\end{bmatrix} $$ The standard matrix for the linear transformation $\mathbf{S}$ is
$S=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 7 \\ 1 & -5\end{bmatrix}$
since it has the following property: $$ \begin{aligned}\overbrace{\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 7 \\ 1 & -5\end{bmatrix}}^{S}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-3\cdot x+7\cdot y \\ 1\cdot x+(-5)\cdot y\end{bmatrix} \\ & =\begin{bmatrix}-3x+7y \\ x-5y\end{bmatrix} \\ & =S\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned} $$ Notice here that $\mathbf{S}$ (using a **bold** letter) denotes the transformation (function) itself, while $S$ (big *italic* letter) is a $2 \times 2$ matrix that corresponds to the linear transformation. In general, the standard matrix of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}: \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} \longrightarrow \begin{bmatrix}{\color{blue}{a}}x+{\color{blue}{b}}y \\ {\color{blue}{c}}x+{\color{blue}{d}}y\end{bmatrix}$ is $$ T=\begin{bmatrix}{\color{blue}{a}} & {\color{blue}{b}} \\ {\color{blue}{c}} & {\color{blue}{d}}\end{bmatrix}. $$ We can learn a lot about linear transformations by looking at their standard matrices.

knowledgePoint.title: Identifying the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation

sections.markdown:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $\mathbf{T},$ where
$$
\mathbf{T}:
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
\longrightarrow 
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}x + 3 y \\ 2 x - y\end{array} \right]}.
$$
sections.title: Identifying the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation
sections.workedSolution:
We require a $2\times 2$ matrix ${T}$ such that
$$
{T} \cdot
    {\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
    =
    {\left[ \begin{array}{c}{\color{blue}1} \cdot  x + {\color{blue}3} \cdot  y \\ {\color{blue}2} \cdot  x + {\color{blue}( - 1 )} \cdot  y\end{array} \right]}.
$$
    Notice that
$$
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}{\color{blue}1} & {\color{blue}3} \\ {\color{blue}2} & {\color{blue}- 1}\end{array} \right]}
	\cdot
    {\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
    =
    {\left[ \begin{array}{c}x + 3 y \\ 2 x - y\end{array} \right]}.
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ is
$$
T=
    {\left[ \begin{array}{cc}1 & 3 \\ 2 & - 1\end{array} \right]}.
$$

knowledgePoint.title: Determining a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix

sections.markdown: What is the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ whose standard matrix is $T={\left[ \begin{array}{cc}8 & - 1 \\ - 5 & - 2\end{array} \right]}?$
sections.title: Determining a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix
sections.workedSolution:
Consider a general vector $\,{\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}.$ Multiplying by the matrix $T,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}8 & -1 \\ -5 & -2\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}8x-y \\ -5x-2y\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\,\mathbf{T}\,$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{T}: {\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]} \longrightarrow {\left[ \begin{array}{c}8 x - y \\ - 5 x - 2 y\end{array} \right]}.
$$

knowledgePoint.title: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix

sections.markdown:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $\mathbf{v}$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ find $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}).$

$$
T={\left[ \begin{array}{cc}4 & 7 \\ - 6 & - 2\end{array} \right]}, \qquad
\mathbf{v}={\left[ \begin{array}{c}- 2 \\ 5\end{array} \right]}.
$$
sections.title: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix
sections.workedSolution:
Using the fact that $\,\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})=T\cdot \mathbf{v},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 7 \\ -6 & -2\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}27 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledgePoint.title: Identifying the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation With Rearranging

sections.markdown:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $\mathbf{T},$ where
$$
\mathbf{T}:
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
\longrightarrow 
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}4 y - 5 x \\ y + 3 x\end{array} \right]}.
$$
sections.title: Identifying the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation With Rearranging
sections.workedSolution:
First, rewrite the order of the variables in the usual way:

$$
\mathbf{T}:
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
\longrightarrow 
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}- 5 x + 4 y \\ 3 x + y\end{array} \right]}
$$

We require a $2\times 2$ matrix ${T}$ such that
$$
{T}\cdot
    {\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
    =
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}- 5 x + 4 y \\ 3 x + y\end{array} \right]}.
$$

Notice that
$$
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}- 5 & 4 \\ 3 & 1\end{array} \right]}
	\cdot
    {\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
    =
    {\left[ \begin{array}{c}- 5 x + 4 y \\ 3 x + y\end{array} \right]}.
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ is
$$
T=
    {\left[ \begin{array}{cc}- 5 & 4 \\ 3 & 1\end{array} \right]}.
$$
